BiblicalUsage: Cumi is the Aramaic word for "arise," and it survives in the New Testament only inside Jesus' own words to the dead girl in Mark 5:41: "Talitha cumi," damsel, arise. The Greek text keeps the Aramaic just as Jesus spoke it, then translates it for the reader.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from it is that the word is precious because it is Jesus' voice, untranslated: a command spoken to death itself, and death obeyed.
